intro: Having bathed and worn a clean dhoti, sit or squat in kukkuṭāsana facing east, with a small vessel of water and an uddharaṇi (spoon). Fold the right palm so that the little, ring and middle fingers are stretched and the index finger is bent inwards, forming a hollow; pour a small amount of water into it and swallow (do not sip) from the brāhma-tīrtha (base of the thumb) with each of the three names, for the purification of body, speech and mind. Then wash the right hand, wipe the lips with the right thumb from right to left, and wash the hand again. Direction: face east in the morning and at noon; in the evening face east until arghya-pradānam and west thereafter (Kidambi, Chakravarthy).

items.action: pour a little water into the right palm and swallow it
items.meaning: Salutations to Acyuta, the unfallen, unchanging one.

items.action: again pour water and swallow
items.meaning: Salutations to Ananta, the infinite one.

items.action: again pour water and swallow; then wash the right hand and wipe the lips with the thumb
items.meaning: Salutations to Govinda, protector of the cows and of the earth.

title.en: Touching the limbs with the twelve names

intro: Touch the parts of the body indicated with the fingers of the right hand while saying each name, consecrating the body as the temple of God. In each case the thumb touches the middle of the finger used (Chakravarthy). Together with the three sips this forms one ācamanam.

items.action: right thumb → right cheek (seat of fire)
items.meaning: Salutations to Keśava, of beautiful locks, slayer of the demon Keśī.

items.action: right thumb → left cheek
items.meaning: Salutations to Nārāyaṇa, the abode and resting place of all beings.

items.action: ring finger → right eye (seat of the Sun)
items.meaning: Salutations to Mādhava, consort of Lakṣmī (Mā).

items.action: ring finger → left eye
items.meaning: Salutations to Govinda, protector of the cows and of the earth.

items.action: index finger → right side of the nose (seat of wind)
items.meaning: Salutations to Viṣṇu, the all-pervading.

items.action: index finger → left side of the nose
items.meaning: Salutations to Madhusūdana, slayer of the demon Madhu.

items.action: little finger → right ear (seat of Indra)
items.meaning: Salutations to Trivikrama, who measured the worlds in three strides.

items.action: little finger → left ear
items.meaning: Salutations to Vāmana, the dwarf incarnation.

items.action: middle finger → right shoulder (seat of Prajāpati)
items.meaning: Salutations to Śrīdhara, bearer of Śrī on His chest.

items.action: middle finger → left shoulder
items.meaning: Salutations to Hṛṣīkeśa, lord of the senses.

items.action: all fingers of the right hand → navel
items.meaning: Salutations to Padmanābha, from whose navel the lotus (of creation) springs.

items.action: all fingers of the right hand → top of the head
items.meaning: Salutations to Dāmodara, who was bound with a rope (dāma) around the waist by Yaśodā.

items.text: Kidambi: this whole ācamanam (three sips and the twelve names) is performed twice.

intro: Gently tap both temples with the knuckles (five times in all, once after each phrase marked in the verse), with the thought that the spiritual nectar collected there is spreading through the body. Kidambi's Śrī Vaiṣṇava text omits this step; the Chakravarthy text notes that *viṣṇum* here refers to Gaṇapati (the obstacle-remover).

text.iast:
śuklāmbaradharaṃ viṣṇuṃ śaśivarṇaṃ caturbhujam |
prasannavadanaṃ dhyāyet sarvavighnopaśāntaye ||

items.action: tap the temples with the fists
items.meaning: The all-pervading Lord Viṣṇu is to be meditated upon for the removal of all obstacles — clad in white garments, resplendent like the moon, four-armed and cheerful-faced.

text.iast:
śuklāmbaradharaṃ viṣṇuṃ śaśivarṇaṃ caturbhujam |
prasannavadanaṃ dhyāyet sarvavighnopaśāntaye ||

items.action: tap the temples with the fists (only if your family does this; Kidambi omits it)
items.meaning: The all-pervading Lord Viṣṇu is to be meditated upon for the removal of all obstacles — clad in white garments, resplendent like the moon, four-armed and cheerful-faced.

intro: Sit erect. Fold the index and middle fingers of the right hand into the palm; the thumb closes the right nostril and the ring and little fingers the left. Close the left nostril and breathe out slowly through the right; close the right nostril, open the left and breathe in fully; then close both nostrils and, with mouth and eyes closed, recite the mantra mentally while holding the breath; open the right nostril and breathe out slowly. Chakravarthy: recite the seven vyāhṛtis while inhaling, the Gāyatrī while holding, and *oṃ āpo jyotī…* while exhaling (ratio 1:3:2). This is one prāṇāyāma; do three. The left hand rests palm-up on the left thigh (thumb and index touching).

text.iast:
oṃ bhūḥ | oṃ bhuvaḥ | oguṃ suvaḥ | oṃ mahaḥ | oṃ janaḥ | oṃ tapaḥ | oguṃ sa̱tyam |
oṃ tat sa̍vi̱tur vare̎ṇya̱ṃ bhargo̍ de̱vasya̍ dhīmahi | dhiyo̱ yo na̍ḥ praco̱dayā̎t ||
oṃ āpo̱ jyotī̱ raso̱'mṛta̱ṃ brahma̱ bhūr bhuva̱ssuva̱rom ||

items.action: recite mentally while holding the breath (three prāṇāyāmas)
items.meaning: Om — the material world; Om — the realm of mind; Om — the realm of light; Om — the realm of vastness; Om — the realm of creative delight; Om — the realm of unobstructed will; Om — the realm of the highest Truth. May we meditate upon that adorable light of the divine Creator; may He impel our intellect. He is in the waters, in light, in flavour, in the nectar of immortality; He pervades the three realms — physical, mental and spiritual. All this is denoted by the Praṇava.

items.text: Then touch the right ear with the fingers of the right hand (śrotrācamanam — Gaṅgā resides in the right ear), and make brahmāñjali: left palm upturned on the right thigh, right palm downturned clasping it. This is also the saṅkalpa posture.

intro: In the saṅkalpa posture (left palm upturned on the right thigh, right palm covering it), state the intent for this sandhyā. Smārtas use the *mamopātta…* form, Śrī Vaiṣṇavas the *śrī bhagavadājñayā…* form. If detailed saṅkalpam is switched on, the day's pañcāṅga (year, ayana, ṛtu, month, pakṣa, tithi, vāra, nakṣatra) is inserted before the kāla. Afterwards wash the right palm with water (Chakravarthy).

text.iast: mamopātta samasta duritakṣaya dvārā śrī parameśvara prītyarthaṃ {panchanga}{kala} sandhyām upāsiṣye ||

items.meaning: For the destruction of all the sins I have accumulated and to please the Supreme Lord, I now perform my {kalaEn} sandhyā worship.

text.iast: śrī bhagavadājñayā śrīmannārāyaṇa prītyarthaṃ {panchanga}{kala} sandhyām upāsiṣye ||

items.meaning: By the command of the Lord and to please Śrīman Nārāyaṇa, I now perform my {kalaEn} sandhyā worship.

title.en: Dedication of the act to the Lord (opening)

intro: With both hands in añjali mudrā (namaste), surrender the agency and fruit of the act to the Lord: He, the indweller, causes this sandhyāvandanam to be done through you, with His own instruments, for His own pleasure.

text.iast: bhagavāneva svaniyāmya svarūpasthiti pravṛtti svaśeṣataika rasena anena ātmanā kartrā svakīyaiśca upakaraṇaiḥ svārādhanaika prayojanāya paramapuruṣaḥ sarvaśeṣī śriyaḥ patiḥ svaśeṣabhūtaṃ idaṃ {kala} sandhyāvandanākhyaṃ karma svasmai svaprītaye svayameva kārayati ||

items.action: hands in añjali
items.meaning: The Lord Himself — the Supreme Person, the master of all, the consort of Śrī — through this self as agent, whose nature, existence and activity are controlled by Him and whose sole delight is being His servant, and with instruments that are His own, for the sole purpose of His own worship, Himself causes this act called the {kalaEn} sandhyāvandanam, which belongs to Him, to be performed for His own sake and for His own pleasure.

intro: If the ūrdhva-puṇḍram or tilakam was not applied after the bath, apply it now: dip the ring finger in water from the vessel, trace *oṃ keśavāya namaḥ* on the water, and apply the mark to the middle of the forehead while reciting.

items.action: apply the tilakam to the forehead with the wet ring finger
items.meaning: Om, salutations to Śrī Keśava.

intro: Hold the vessel in the left hand; take a little water in the right palm (or on the ring finger from the uddharaṇi) and sprinkle it on the head with the fingers of the right hand, once with each line. Nyāsa first: touch the top of the head while naming the ṛṣi, the tip of the nose for the chandas, the heart for the devatā, and join the palms in añjali for the viniyoga (Kidambi, Chakravarthy).

text.iast: āpo hiṣṭheti mantrasya sindhudvīpa ṛṣiḥ | devī gāyatrī chandaḥ | āpo devatā | apāṃ prokṣaṇe viniyogaḥ ||

items.action: nyāsa: touch head (ṛṣi), tip of nose (chandas), heart (devatā); then añjali (viniyoga)
items.meaning: Of the mantra *āpo hiṣṭhā*, Sindhudvīpa is the seer, devī gāyatrī the metre, the Waters the deity; it is applied in the sprinkling of water.

text.iast:
oṃ bhūr bhuva̱ssuva̍ḥ |
tat sa̍vi̱tur vare̎ṇya̱ṃ bhargo̍ de̱vasya̍ dhīmahi |
dhiyo̱ yo na̍ḥ praco̱dayā̎t ||

items.action: prelude (Kidambi): sprinkle on the head three times, once with each line
items.meaning: Om, earth, atmosphere, heaven. May we meditate upon that adorable light of the divine Savitṛ; may He impel our thoughts.

text.iast:
āpo̱ hiṣṭhā ma̍yo̱ bhuva̍ḥ | tā na̍ ū̱rje da̍dhātana | ma̱he raṇā̍ya̱ cakṣa̍se |
yo va̍śśi̱vata̍mo̱ rasa̍ḥ | tasya̍ bhājayate̱ha na̍ḥ | u̱śa̱tīri̍va mā̱tara̍ḥ |
tasmā̱ ara̍ṅga māma vaḥ |

items.action: sprinkle on the head once with each of these seven lines
items.meaning: O Waters, you are indeed the source of bliss; grant us nourishment, that we may behold great delight. Grant us here a share of that most auspicious essence of yours, like mothers in their tender love. To Him we come gladly, (to whose abode you lead us).

items.action: sprinkle on the big toes
items.meaning: …for whose abode you quicken us.

items.action: sprinkle again on the head
items.meaning: O Waters, make us pure and grant us to be reborn with splendour.

items.action: take a little water in the palm and circle it around the head clockwise, sprinkling it around yourself
items.meaning: Om, earth, atmosphere, heaven.

intro: Nyāsa as before (head – nose – heart – añjali). Then pour a small amount of water into the hollow of the right palm, recite the mantra for the kāla, and swallow (do not sip) the water from the brahma-tīrtha. Afterwards perform ācamanam.

text.iast: sūryaścety anuvākasya agnir ṛṣiḥ | devī gāyatrī chandaḥ | sūryo devatā | apāṃ prāśane viniyogaḥ ||

items.action: nyāsa: touch head (ṛṣi), tip of nose (chandas), heart (devatā); then añjali (viniyoga)
items.meaning: Of the anuvāka beginning *sūryaśca*, Agni is the seer, devī gāyatrī the metre, Sūrya the deity; it is applied in the sipping of water.

text.iast: sūryaśca mā manyuśca manyupatayaśca manyu̍kṛte̱bhyaḥ | pāpebhyo̍ rakṣa̱ntām | yad rātriyā pāpa̍m akā̱rṣam | manasā vācā̍ hastā̱bhyām | padbhyām udare̍ṇa śi̱śnā | rātri̱s tad ava̍lu̱mpatu | yat kiñca̍ duri̱taṃ mayi̍ | idam ahaṃ mām amṛ̍ta yo̱nau | sūrye jyotiṣi juho̍mi svā̱hā ||

items.action: recite with the water in the right palm, then swallow it
items.meaning: May the Sun, anger, the lords of anger and (the deities presiding over) the sins born of anger protect me. Whatever sin I have committed by night — by thought, speech, hands, feet, belly or organ — may the night efface it. Whatever evil remains in me, I offer myself as an oblation into the Sun, the source of immortality, the Light. Svāhā.

text.iast: āpaḥ punantv ity anuvākasya āpa ṛṣiḥ | anuṣṭup chandaḥ | brahmaṇaspatir devatā | apāṃ prāśane viniyogaḥ ||

items.action: nyāsa: touch head (ṛṣi), tip of nose (chandas), heart (devatā); then añjali (viniyoga)
items.meaning: Of the anuvāka beginning *āpaḥ punantu*, the Waters are the seer, anuṣṭup the metre, Brahmaṇaspati the deity; it is applied in the sipping of water.

text.iast: āpa̍ḥ punantu pṛthi̱vīṃ pṛ̍thi̱vī pū̱tā pu̍nātu̱ mām | pu̱nantu̱ brahma̍ṇa̱spati̱r brahma̍ pū̱tā pu̍nātu̱ mām | yad ucchi̍ṣṭa̱m abho̎jya̱ṃ yad vā̍ du̱ścari̍ta̱ṃ mama̍ | sarva̍ṃ punantu̱ mām āpo̍'sa̱tāṃ ca̍ prati̱graha̱guṃ svāhā̎ ||

items.action: recite with the water in the right palm, then swallow it
items.meaning: May the waters purify the earth; may the purified earth purify me. May the Lord of prayer purify me; may the purified Veda purify me. Whatever remnant I have eaten, whatever forbidden food, whatever misdeed of mine, whatever gift accepted from the unworthy — may the waters purify me of all. Svāhā.

text.iast: agniścety anuvākasya sūrya ṛṣiḥ | devī gāyatrī chandaḥ | agnir devatā | apāṃ prāśane viniyogaḥ ||

items.action: nyāsa: touch head (ṛṣi), tip of nose (chandas), heart (devatā); then añjali (viniyoga)
items.meaning: Of the anuvāka beginning *agniśca*, Sūrya is the seer, devī gāyatrī the metre, Agni the deity; it is applied in the sipping of water.

text.iast: agniśca mā manyuśca manyupatayaśca manyu̍kṛte̱bhyaḥ | pāpebhyo̍ rakṣa̱ntām | yad ahnā pāpa̍m akā̱rṣam | manasā vācā̍ hastā̱bhyām | padbhyām udare̍ṇa śi̱śnā | aha̱s tad ava̍lu̱mpatu | yat kiñca̍ duri̱taṃ mayi̍ | idam ahaṃ mām amṛ̍ta yo̱nau | satye jyotiṣi juho̍mi svā̱hā ||

items.action: recite with the water in the right palm, then swallow it
items.meaning: May Agni, anger, the lords of anger and (the deities presiding over) the sins born of anger protect me. Whatever sin I have committed by day — by thought, speech, hands, feet, belly or organ — may the day efface it. Whatever evil remains in me, I offer myself as an oblation into Truth, the source of immortality, the Light. Svāhā.

items.text: Then perform ācamanam (three sips with *acyutāya, anantāya, govindāya namaḥ* and the twelve names).

intro: Nyāsa as before. Then sprinkle water on the head with the *dadhikrāvṇṇo* verse, and repeat the sprinkling with *āpo hiṣṭhā* exactly as in prokṣaṇam.

text.iast: dadhikrāvṇṇa iti mantrasya vāmadeva ṛṣiḥ | anuṣṭup chandaḥ | dadhikrāvā devatā | apāṃ prokṣaṇe viniyogaḥ ||

items.action: nyāsa: touch head (ṛṣi), tip of nose (chandas), heart (devatā); then añjali (viniyoga)
items.meaning: Of the mantra *dadhikrāvṇṇo*, Vāmadeva is the seer, anuṣṭup the metre, Dadhikrāvan the deity; it is applied in the sprinkling of water.

text.iast:
da̱dhi̱krāvṇṇo̍ akāriṣaṃ ji̱ṣṇor aśva̍sya vā̱jina̍ḥ |
su̱ra̱bhi no̱ mukhā̍ kara̱t praṇa̱ āyū̍guṃṣi tāriṣat ||

items.action: sprinkle on the head once with each of the four pādas
items.meaning: I have glorified Dadhikrāvan, the victorious, swift steed (the Lord as Hayagrīva). May He make our mouths fragrant and lengthen our lives. (RV 4.39.6; TS 1.5.11.4)

text.iast:
āpo̱ hiṣṭhā ma̍yo̱ bhuva̍ḥ | tā na̍ ū̱rje da̍dhātana | ma̱he raṇā̍ya̱ cakṣa̍se |
yo va̍śśi̱vata̍mo̱ rasa̍ḥ | tasya̍ bhājayate̱ha na̍ḥ | u̱śa̱tīri̍va mā̱tara̍ḥ |
tasmā̱ ara̍ṅga māma vaḥ |

items.action: sprinkle on the head once with each of these seven lines
items.meaning: O Waters, you are indeed the source of bliss; grant us nourishment, that we may behold great delight. Grant us here a share of that most auspicious essence of yours, like mothers in their tender love. To Him we come gladly, (to whose abode you lead us).

items.action: sprinkle on the big toes
items.meaning: …for whose abode you quicken us.

items.action: sprinkle again on the head
items.meaning: O Waters, make us pure and grant us to be reborn with splendour.

items.action: take a little water in the palm and circle it around the head clockwise, sprinkling it around yourself
items.meaning: Om, earth, atmosphere, heaven.

intro: Perform prāṇāyāma (Chakravarthy: one round), touch the right ear, and take the saṅkalpa posture for the saṅkalpa; then nyāsa. Stand erect (morning and noon facing east; in the evening face west from now on) holding the vessel between the thumb and index finger of the left hand; join both palms facing upwards, pour water into the hollow of the joined palms and raise them to the level of the forehead. Recite the Gāyatrī aloud and, looking towards the sun and rising on the heels, release the water from the fingertips (deva-tīrtha), thrown up towards the sun; if standing in a river or tank, offer with cupped palms. Three libations in the morning and evening; at noon one (Kidambi, who notes that some sampradāyas offer two). Chakravarthy: at noon standing or sitting; in the evening sitting.

text.iast:
oṃ bhūḥ | oṃ bhuvaḥ | oguṃ suvaḥ | oṃ mahaḥ | oṃ janaḥ | oṃ tapaḥ | oguṃ sa̱tyam |
oṃ tat sa̍vi̱tur vare̎ṇya̱ṃ bhargo̍ de̱vasya̍ dhīmahi | dhiyo̱ yo na̍ḥ praco̱dayā̎t ||
oṃ āpo̱ jyotī̱ raso̱'mṛta̱ṃ brahma̱ bhūr bhuva̱ssuva̱rom ||

items.action: prāṇāyāma as before (recite mentally holding the breath); then touch the right ear and take the saṅkalpa posture
items.meaning: Om — the seven realms; may we meditate upon that adorable light of the divine Creator, may He impel our intellect; He is the waters, light, flavour, immortality, Brahman, pervading the three worlds — Om.

text.iast: mamopātta samasta duritakṣaya dvārā śrī parameśvara prītyarthaṃ {kala} sandhyā sūryārghya pradānaṃ kariṣye ||

items.meaning: For the destruction of all my sins and to please the Supreme Lord, I now offer the {kalaEn} sandhyā libations of water to the Sun.

text.iast: śrī bhagavadājñayā śrīmannārāyaṇa prītyarthaṃ {kala} sandhyā arghyapradānaṃ kariṣye ||

items.meaning: By the command of the Lord and to please Śrīman Nārāyaṇa, I now offer the {kalaEn} sandhyā libations of water (to the Sun).

text.iast: arghyapradāna mantrasya viśvāmitra ṛṣiḥ | devī gāyatrī chandaḥ | savitā devatā | arghyapradāne viniyogaḥ ||

items.action: nyāsa: touch head (ṛṣi), tip of nose (chandas), heart (devatā); then añjali (viniyoga)
items.meaning: Of the arghya mantra, Viśvāmitra is the seer, devī gāyatrī the metre, Savitṛ the deity; it is applied in the offering of arghya.

text.iast: oṃ bhūr bhuva̱ssuva̍ḥ | tat sa̍vi̱tur vare̎ṇya̱ṃ bhargo̍ de̱vasya̍ dhīmahi | dhiyo̱ yo na̍ḥ praco̱dayā̎t ||

items.action: stand, water in the joined palms raised to the forehead; recite, rise on the heels looking at the sun and release the water from the fingertips — once per libation
items.meaning: Om, earth, atmosphere, heaven. We meditate upon that adorable light of the divine Savitṛ; may He impel our thoughts.

items.action: after each libation
items.meaning: Om, salutations to the Sun — this is the libation.

intro: If the sandhyā is being performed after the prescribed time (after sunrise in the morning, after sunset in the evening; at noon only in some sampradāyas — Kidambi), an extra fourth libation is offered as atonement. Prāṇāyāma, śrotrācamanam and the saṅkalpa posture; saṅkalpa; nyāsa; then, standing as before with water in the joined palms raised to the forehead, recite and release the water once, rising on the heels and looking towards the sun.

items.text: Prāṇāyāma as before (*oṃ bhūḥ … bhūr bhuvas suvarom*), touch the right ear, then the saṅkalpa posture.

text.iast: mamopātta samasta duritakṣaya dvārā śrī parameśvara prītyarthaṃ {kala} sandhyā kālātīta prāyaścittārthaṃ turīyārghya pradānaṃ kariṣye ||

items.meaning: For the destruction of all my sins and to please the Supreme Lord, I now offer a fourth libation to the Sun to atone for performing my {kalaEn} sandhyā after the prescribed time.

text.iast: śrī bhagavadājñayā śrīmannārāyaṇa prītyarthaṃ {kala} sandhyā kālātīta doṣa prāyaścittārthaṃ turīya arghyapradānaṃ kariṣye ||

items.meaning: By the command of the Lord and to please Śrīman Nārāyaṇa, I now offer a fourth libation to atone for the fault of performing my {kalaEn} sandhyā after the prescribed time.

text.iast: turīya arghyapradāna mantrasya sāndīpanī ṛṣiḥ | devī gāyatrī chandaḥ | savitā devatā | turīya arghyapradāne viniyogaḥ ||

items.action: nyāsa: touch head (ṛṣi), tip of nose (chandas), heart (devatā); then añjali (viniyoga)
items.meaning: Of the fourth-arghya mantra, Sāndīpanī is the seer, devī gāyatrī the metre, Savitṛ the deity; it is applied in offering the fourth arghya.

text.iast:
oṃ bhūḥ | oṃ bhuvaḥ | oguṃ suvaḥ | oṃ mahaḥ | oṃ janaḥ | oṃ tapaḥ | oguṃ sa̱tyam |
oṃ tat sa̍vi̱tur vare̎ṇya̱ṃ bhargo̍ de̱vasya̍ dhīmahi | dhiyo̱ yo na̍ḥ praco̱dayā̎t |
oṃ bhūḥ | oṃ bhuvaḥ | oguṃ suvaḥ | oṃ mahaḥ | oṃ janaḥ | oṃ tapaḥ | oguṃ sa̱tyam ||

items.action: offer the single extra libation with the vyāhṛtis, the Gāyatrī and the vyāhṛtis again
items.meaning: Om — the seven realms. May we meditate upon that adorable light of the divine Savitṛ; may He impel our thoughts. Om — the seven realms.

title.en: Circling oneself; contemplation of the Sun as Brahman

intro: Take a little water in the right palm and, reciting *oṃ bhūr bhuvas suvaḥ*, circle the hand around the head clockwise while turning yourself once clockwise on the spot, letting the water fall around you. Then, standing facing the sun with hands in añjali, meditate on the Lord in the centre of the Sun and on the meaning of the sentence for a minute or two, eyes closed. Do not rush this.

items.action: circle the water around the head clockwise while turning yourself clockwise (ātma-pradakṣiṇam)
items.meaning: Om, earth, atmosphere, heaven.

items.action: hands in añjali; contemplate the Lord in the centre of the Sun
items.meaning: Yonder Sun is Brahman.

items.action: meditate for a while that you and Brahman are the same
items.meaning: Brahman indeed am I.

intro: Sit in kukkuṭāsana and perform ācamanam again: swallow water three times with the three names, then touch the limbs with the twelve names.

items.action: pour a little water into the right palm and swallow it
items.meaning: Salutations to Acyuta, the unfallen, unchanging one.

items.action: again pour water and swallow
items.meaning: Salutations to Ananta, the infinite one.

items.action: again pour water and swallow; wash the hand and wipe the lips
items.meaning: Salutations to Govinda, protector of the cows and of the earth.

text.iast: oṃ keśavāya namaḥ | oṃ nārāyaṇāya namaḥ | oṃ mādhavāya namaḥ | oṃ govindāya namaḥ | oṃ viṣṇave namaḥ | oṃ madhusūdanāya namaḥ | oṃ trivikramāya namaḥ | oṃ vāmanāya namaḥ | oṃ śrīdharāya namaḥ | oṃ hṛṣīkeśāya namaḥ | oṃ padmanābhāya namaḥ | oṃ dāmodarāya namaḥ ||

items.action: thumb → right, left cheek; ring finger → right, left eye; index → right, left side of nose; little finger → right, left ear; middle finger → right, left shoulder; all fingers → navel, top of head
items.meaning: Salutations to Keśava, Nārāyaṇa, Mādhava, Govinda, Viṣṇu, Madhusūdana, Trivikrama, Vāmana, Śrīdhara, Hṛṣīkeśa, Padmanābha and Dāmodara.

title.en: Libations to the planets and the twelve names

intro: Sit in kukkuṭāsana holding the vessel between the thumb and index finger of the left hand; join both palms facing upwards. For each name pour water into the hollow of the joined palms, recite, and let the water flow out through the fingertips of both hands (deva-tīrtha) onto the ground or plate — like arghya but without rising on the heels. Smārtas offer to the nine grahas and then the twelve names; Śrī Vaiṣṇavas (Kidambi) to the twelve names only.

items.text: Then perform ācamanam (three sips and the twelve names).

items.meaning: Om, That is the Truth — may this be an offering to Brahman.

title.en: Sprinkling the place of japa; the seat mantra

intro: Sprinkle a little water on a clean spot for the japa with *oṃ bhūr bhuvas suvaḥ*. Stand in the sprinkled area facing east — west in the evening. Nyāsa (head – nose – heart – añjali), then recite the seat mantra with hands in añjali. Some Smārtas first add a prayer to the earth to clear the spot of obstructing beings.

items.action: sprinkle water on the place where you will sit for japa
items.meaning: Om, earth, atmosphere, heaven.

text.iast:
apasarpantu te bhūtā ye bhūtā bhūmisaṃsthitāḥ |
ye bhūtā vighnakartāras te gacchantu śivājñayā ||

items.action: bhūmi prārthanā: meditate while reciting
items.meaning: May the beings that dwell on this ground move away; may those beings that cause obstacles depart by the command of Śiva.

text.iast: āsana mantrasya pṛthivyā merupṛṣṭha ṛṣiḥ | sutalaṃ chandaḥ | śrī kūrmo devatā | āsane viniyogaḥ ||

items.action: nyāsa: touch head (ṛṣi), tip of nose (chandas), heart (devatā); then añjali (viniyoga)
items.meaning: Of the seat mantra, Merupṛṣṭha (the back of Mount Meru, addressed to Pṛthivī) is the seer, sutala the metre, Śrī Kūrma (the Tortoise) the deity; it is applied for the seat.

text.iast:
pṛthvi tvayā dhṛtā lokā devi tvaṃ viṣṇunā dhṛtā |
tvaṃ ca dhāraya māṃ devi pavitraṃ kuru cāsanam ||

items.action: hands in añjali
items.meaning: O Mother Earth, by you the worlds are supported, and you, O Goddess, are supported by Viṣṇu. Support me too, O Goddess, and purify this seat.
